answer_verbatim:
If you want **structured online learning** for shadow work, the strongest options in the results are **Jung Platform’s “Introduction to Jungian Shadow Work”**, **Awake Academy’s “Embracing The Shadow”**, and **Shadow Work’s “Basic Facilitator Training Online”** for a more guided, process-oriented path.[3][10][7]

A practical shortlist, depending on your goal:

| Course | Best for | What the results indicate |
|---|---|---|
| **Introduction to Jungian Shadow Work** | Theory + depth psychology | A Jung-oriented introduction, which is useful if you want the classic psychological framework behind shadow work.[3] |
| **Embracing The Shadow** | Spiritual + contemplative practice | Offered by Awake Academy with Charlie Morley, suggesting a more spiritually oriented approach.[10] |
| **Basic Facilitator Training Online** | Structured, step-by-step practice | Designed as a facilitator training, which implies a more formal and methodical process.[7] |
| **Shadow Work: Heal & Integrate your Shadow Self** | Self-paced beginner study | A Udemy course focused on healing and integration, likely suitable for independent learners.[2] |
| **Shadow Mastery Diploma Course** | Broader course + exercises | Appears to be a more extended online program with exercises and a diploma-style structure.[4] |
| **Shadow Work Practitioner Online Certificate Course** | Certification-oriented learning | Best if you want a credentialed course format.[5] |

If your focus is specifically **spiritual practice**, the best match in the results is **Embracing The Shadow** because it is presented through Awake Academy and led by Charlie Morley, which points to a spiritual-development framing rather than only a psychological one.[10]

If your focus is **deepening shadow work as a personal practice**, **Jung Platform** and **Shadow Work’s facilitator training** look like the most structured starting points.[3][7]

A few cautions before enrolling:
- The results mix **serious instructional programs** with **marketing-style course listings**, so it helps to check instructor background, lesson outline, refund policy, and whether the course emphasizes psychology, spirituality, or coaching.[1][11][15]
- If you are new to shadow work, start with a **beginner-friendly course** rather than a facilitator certification or practitioner track.[2][5][7]
